OpenAI Announces GPT-5 With Reasoning Breakthrough

By Kyle Wiggers July 18, 2026

OpenAI today announced GPT-5, its most capable language model to date, featuring what the company describes as a fundamental breakthrough in multi-step reasoning. The model, which has been available to select enterprise partners since May, will begin rolling out to all ChatGPT Plus and Pro subscribers next week.

In a press briefing, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman called GPT-5 "the first model that genuinely feels like it can think through complex problems the way a human expert would." The company claims the model achieves state-of-the-art performance on graduate-level reasoning benchmarks, scoring 92% on the GPQA Diamond test, up from 56% on GPT-4o.

The key technical innovation is what OpenAI calls "structured reasoning chains" — the model's ability to break down complex questions into explicit intermediate steps and verify its own logic before producing a final answer. Internal testing showed GPT-5 reduced hallucination rates by 40% compared to GPT-4o, particularly on questions requiring domain-specific knowledge.

For developers, GPT-5 introduces a new "tool use" API that allows the model to autonomously chain together function calls, search results, and code execution. In demonstrations, the model completed a complex data analysis task that previously required a senior data engineer approximately 45 minutes, doing so in under 3 minutes with comparable accuracy.

The model also shows significant improvements in code generation, particularly for large-scale software projects. On the SWE-Bench Verified benchmark, GPT-5 resolved 53% of real-world GitHub issues autonomously, compared to 22% for the previous best model. OpenAI attributed this improvement to a combination of better training data curation and a novel reinforcement learning approach that rewards complete, test-passing solutions rather than partial code output.

Safety researchers at the model's independent evaluation partner, Apollo Research, noted in a public report that GPT-5 demonstrated "markedly improved alignment" on deception detection tests, though they flagged new concerns about the model's ability to pursue long-term strategies in simulated multi-turn interactions.

OpenAI said GPT-5 will be priced at $30 per million input tokens and $60 per million output tokens for API access, roughly double the cost of GPT-4o. The company framed this as justified by the model's ability to accomplish more per token. "The question isn't cost per token — it's cost per task," said OpenAI CTO Mira Murati.

The announcement intensifies the already fierce competition in the AI industry. Anthropic released Claude 5.1 last week with its own reasoning improvements, and Google's Gemini 2.5 is expected to launch in early August. Meta continues to compete aggressively through open-source releases of its Llama model family.

Industry analysts at Goldman Sachs projected the large language model market would reach $100 billion in annual revenue by 2028, up from an estimated $18 billion in 2026. GPT-5's launch is expected to accelerate enterprise adoption, particularly in legal, healthcare, and financial services where complex reasoning capabilities are essential.

The rollout to ChatGPT Plus and Pro subscribers begins July 22, with enterprise API access available immediately. OpenAI said the model will be available in ChatGPT's free tier "later this year," though no specific timeline was provided.
